rag.name: Matroid.isBinary_iff

/-- `Matroid` is binary iff it can be constructed from a `BinaryMatroid`. -/
lemma Matroid.isBinary_iff [DecidableEq α] (M : Matroid α) : M.IsBinary ↔ ∃ B : BinaryMatroid α, B.toMatroid = M := by
  rfl

Matroid.sum'_isBasis_iff
rag.content:
@[simp] lemma sum'_isBasis_iff {I X} :
    (Matroid.sum' M).IsBasis I X ↔ ∀ i, (M i).IsBasis (Prod.mk i ⁻¹' I) (Prod.mk i ⁻¹' X) := by
  simp [Matroid.sum']
  convert Iff.rfl <;>
  exact ext <| by simp

prescopes: variable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] {M₁ M₂ : Matroid α} [Fintype M₁.E.Elem] [Fintype M₂.E.Elem]
informal_statement: If a regular matroid is a 1-sum of binary matroids, then both of the original matroids being summed are themselves regular.
informal_proof: Suppose we have a regular matroid that is formed as the 1-sum of two binary matroids. To decompose this structure back into its components, we apply the properties of matroid decomposition. By leveraging the fact that the resulting sum is regular and binary, we can deduce that each summand must individually satisfy the regularity conditions. This follows from the inherent properties of regular matroids and their interaction within the 1-sum framework. Thus, both original matroids are proven to be regular.

id.name: Disjoint.decomposition_isRegular_both
id.content:
/-- If a regular matroid is a 1-sum of binary matroids, both summand matroids are regular. -/
lemma Disjoint.decomposition_isRegular_both (hE : M₁.E ⫗ M₂.E) (regularity : hE.build1sum.IsRegular) :
    M₁.IsRegular ∧ M₂.IsRegular :=
  ⟨hE.decomposition_isRegular_left regularity, hE.decomposition_isRegular_right regularity⟩
